cards.text: Grab your apron, friend, because here comes the list of Israel's heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officers who served the king. David's army is split into divisions. And together those divisions have the WHOLE year to cover.

cards.question: David's army divisions had the whole year to cover. How did they serve the king?

answers.text: Each division took its own month
Every division served all year long
Each division served only in wartime

cards.text: Then come the twelve divisions, one for each month, each with 24,000 men and a commander in charge. One name to spot is Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, mighty among the Thirty, who takes the third month. Twelve crews, and every crew knows its month. Friend, I can't even remember what day I last cleaned my oven.
Next comes a list of the leaders over the tribes of Israel, with Zadok, a priest (1 Chronicles 16:39), over Aaron's family too. And over Judah is Elihu, one of David's brothers.
Now the list stops for a census, a count of Israel's men. And David leaves one group out of it.

cards.question: David counted the men of Israel but left one group out. Which men did he leave out of the count?

answers.text: Men over the age of sixty

cards.question: David left the men aged twenty or under out of the count. Why?

answers.text: The LORD said Israel would be as many as the stars
The LORD said only older men would go to battle
The army leaders said they already had plenty of men

cards.question: Joab son of Zeruiah, David's army commander, finished counting the men.
Joab stopped partway through the count. Because of this census, ___ came upon Israel.
The number from Joab's count was never written in the Book of the Chronicles of King David.

cards.text: Next up are the officials in charge of King David's property: his storehouses, his land and his animals. Obil the Ishmaelite gets the camels. Friend, I'm in charge of ONE oven, and some days the oven is STILL winning.

Last come the people around the king himself: counselors like David's uncle Jonathan and Ahithophel, a man who looks after the king's sons, and Joab over the king's army. And Hushai the Archite is listed as the king's friend. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer beside an expired coupon, and NOBODY ever wrote down that we were friends.
